Evidence caveats

  • 15,276 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.

Evidence caveats

  • 1,848 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 1,848 games at 63.0%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 34,968 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 34,968 games at 71.2%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

The causal slot verdict is node cli.js roster-ablate <team> <slot>.

  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. Evidence caveats

  • 462 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 462 games at 63.0%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 1,548 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 1,548 games at 61.8%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 20,618 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.

The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.

  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 20,618 games at 65.3%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

  • 15,930 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.

The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.

  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.

Evidence caveats

  • 1,038 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.

The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.

  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.

  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. Evidence caveats

  • 4,938 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.

The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.

  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 4,938 games at 62.9%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.
